messages:
maya: Quick sync — Orchid Health hit another on‑prem VPC isolation this morning (08:12 UTC). Root cause looks consistent with the stale peering + ingress kernel reload race we saw last quarter. I sketched a short postmortem and want to align owners/timeline for a remediation sweep. Link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/orchid-isolation-draft :memo:

devin: saw the alert. flapping window 08:10–08:14, infra-bot fired 08:11. I'll put together the alert tuning and a recurring check. provisional owners: liam (peering), sophia (kernel/ingress), maya (coord).

liam: +1. I'll own the peering hardening. Plan: add route validation, peer TTL, and a graceful peer health probe. Target: canary in dedicated staging by EOD Fri. Steps in brief: 1) validate route diffs on BGP updates 2) enforce TTL on peering entries 3) emit telemetry metric peer_stale_count.

sophia: I can take the kernel/ingress side. I suspect an iptables/netstack reload race causing cached routes to drop. Need a reproducible test — can someone provide access to the Orchid staging overlay? @maya

maya: Orchid staging access requested and sec approved. I added a short repro doc in the postmortem. Timeline suggestion: patch in staging Thu, canary Fri, roll Mon. Also propose a 6‑week followup cadence (weekly check-ins) to watch for recurrences.

devin: I'll add alert changes: new alert isolate_incidents > 3 in 1h -> pager. Also creating a recurring 'isolation-sweep' calendar invite for the team (weekly for 6 weeks). Will file a ticket for runbook updates.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1473. Severity: P2. First alert: 2026-03-20T08:11:26Z. Attached logs: /incidents/INC-2026-1473/logs.tar.gz

liam: quick ops snippet for debugging Orchid: ```ssh jump@orchid-staging -- sudo ip route show proto static | grep peer``` will show stale peer entries. I'll add a small script to auto-detect and alert on anomalies.

sophia: reproduced in staging using the repro doc. Found a timing window during systemd-networkd reload where iptables flush + route re-add race occurs. Pushing branch: fix/iptables-reload-guard. Will open PR and request net-eng review.

maya: Action items (summary) — please acknowledge: 1) liam — peering hardening (route validation + TTL + telemetry). ETA 2026-03-27. 2) sophia — kernel/iptables reload guard and PR. ETA 2026-03-26. 3) devin — alert tuning + recurring check-in invite + runbook updates. ETA 2026-03-24. 4) maya — coordinate customer comms + finalize postmortem. ETA 2026-03-25. Weekly check-in: Wed 10:00 PT for 6 weeks. Please ack with a quick reply. :white_check_mark:

liam: ack :thumbsup:

devin: ack, adding tickets and invite now.

sophia: ack, PR opened and flagged for review (net-eng).

maya: added to remediation tracker: https://redwood.track/runs/ORB-412. I also linked the postmortem and the canary playbook. We'll use the tracker to record progress and regression results.

devin: PR/runs to reference in tracker: run 2026-03-21 orch-staging-ci #78, runbook PR #412. I'll attach alert diffs as a patch.

maya: re: recurring patterns — dev note: if we see >2 customer isolations of this class in 30d, we escalate to a cross-team task force (eng-runtime + infra + platform). Adding a badge to the tracker for that condition.

infra-bot: Reminder scheduled: Weekly check-in created for "isolation sweep" starting 2026-03-24 17:00Z.

liam: leaving a small post-PR test checklist: 1) canary peering for 24h 2) metric peer_stale_count <= 0 for 24h 3) no new isolate_incidents alerts.

sophia: will run kernel config experiment in canary and report results in tracker.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll update the postmortem with these action items and send a brief to Orchid support. If anyone hits blockers, post here and I'll escalate.
